title: M1: a yes/no probability per family, and up to three answers per sentence
question: A sentence often describes two or three techniques but carries one label. If every family gets its own yes/no probability, instead of a share of one answer, do up to three answers per sentence find the labelled technique more often than the same rule on the one-answer model, at the same number of answers?
motivation: Owner's request (2026-10-14): accept up to three families/techniques per sentence when the model is confident enough. On E2's dev predictions the one-answer model puts nearly all probability on one family (second family median 0.05; a second labelled family median 0.03), so a confidence threshold barely adds answers, and only 8% of the 61 dev sentences with several labelled families get all of them among up to three answers. A reading of 24 dev mistakes found 11 where the sentence supports both the label and the model's answer; CTI-HAL was annotated by two people on separate reports, one technique per statement in most cases (66 of 968 carry several).
harness: family_head.py --family-loss yesno --negative-weight 0.1; losses.yes_no; multi_answer.py (scorer, standard library); runpod/remote_m1.sh

model.family_probability: sigmoid(logit) per family, independent of the others (E2: softmax over the 222 families)
model.loss: losses.yes_no: sum over labelled families of -log P + 0.1 x sum over every other family of -log(1 - P). A missing label is weak evidence of 'no': at the optimum a family labelled on a share q of the sentences that look alike scores q / (q + 0.1 (1 - q)), so a technique labelled on 1 in 5 of the sentences that show it still scores about 0.7.
model.starting_bias: one shared bias = minus the median second-highest logit over 64 training sentences (seed 7), so a typical sentence starts with only its top family above 0.5; without it the untrained cosine head put dozens of families above 0.9 (laptop pilot)
model.techniques: unchanged from E1/E2: P(technique | family) is a softmax within the family; an answer family's technique is its most probable one
model.fixed: E2's data (26,353 rows), recipe and selection rule (mean of public dev exact top-1 and AnnoCTR dev family top-1 under the one-answer rule), 2 epochs, checkpoint every quarter epoch, seed 7; RunPod secure RTX 4090; CTI-HAL scored on the laptop

answer_rule.rule: the most probable family, plus the second and third when their probability reaches the threshold (multi_family.families_named, up to 3), each with its most probable technique
answer_rule.threshold: per model and split, the value that gives 1.3 answers per sentence on average, set from the model's own probabilities without labels (multi_answer.budget_threshold); both models are compared at the same number of answers
answer_rule.budget: 1.3 answers per sentence (the owner was offered 1.1 / 1.3 / 1.5; on E2's dev, 1.3 is a threshold of about 0.14 and gives a second or third answer to about 1 sentence in 4)
answer_rule.hit: a labelled family (family hit) or a labelled technique (exact hit) among the answers

baseline: E2 (data/models/cribl_ft/E2/step_52706) with the same answer rule and budget. On dev at 1.3: family hit 0.803, exact hit 0.715 (one answer: 0.734 / 0.651).

success.headline: CTI-HAL family hit at 1.3 answers per sentence: M1 minus E2 (same 968 statements), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: CTI-HAL exact hit at 1.3: M1 minus E2, CI lower bound above 0
CTI-HAL one-answer family top-1 not worse: M1 minus E2, CI lower bound above -0.02
public test and AnnoCTR test family hit at 1.3: M1 minus E2, CI lower bound above 0
success.reported: the 66 CTI-HAL statements with several labelled families: share with all of them among the answers, and answers per sentence on several-label vs one-label statements (does the number of answers follow the sentence); M1 at a fixed threshold of 0.5 (answers per sentence and hits: the owner's 'clears a confidence threshold' reading); budgets 1.1 and 1.5; extra answers matching a label; family micro precision/recall/F1; every checkpoint's dev numbers under both rules

blind_check: reported, not a gate: 100 extra answers on CTI-HAL at 1.3 (50 from each model, drawn with seed 7, shuffled, model hidden in a separate key) judged 'supported by the sentence' or not by Claude from the sentence and the technique name only; one AI reader, stated as such
stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
informed_by: E2's dev and confirmation predictions (docs 21.3.18) and the dev threshold table shown to the owner; the 24-mistake dev reading; the CTI-HAL paper's annotation description (arXiv 2504.05866); a laptop pilot (100 rows, 30 dev cases; mechanics and the starting bias only). No M1 model exists.
